# Didache Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 7

**1** Concerning baptism: baptize in the following way. After you have rehearsed all of the foregoing, baptize in running water, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

**2** If you do not have running water, baptize in other water; if you cannot use cold water, use warm.

**3** But if you have neither, pour water over the head three times, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

**4** Before the baptism, let the one who baptizes and the one being baptized fast — and any others who are able. Require the one being baptized to fast for one or two days beforehand.

---

*LOGOS notes: This is the earliest Christian baptismal instruction outside the New Testament. The order of preference (running water → still water → affusion) accommodates diverse circumstances. "Running water" (ὕδωρ ζῶν, "living water") has roots in Jewish purity practice (mikveh regulations preferred running water). The instruction "after you have rehearsed all of the foregoing" (ταῦτα πάντα προειπόντες) refers to the Two Ways teaching — the Didache presents the entire ethical catechism as pre-baptismal preparation. The trinitarian formula (Father/Son/Holy Spirit) matches Matthew 28:19, suggesting a common liturgical tradition. Pre-baptismal fasting by both administrator and candidate is noteworthy — baptism was a solemn communal event.*
